sources.title: For the Right Reasons: The FORR Architecture for Learning in a Skill Domain
sources.access: Publisher free-access abstract; methods not reviewed
sources.institution: Hunter College and CUNY Graduate School

sources.title: Learning Expertise with Bounded Rationality and Self-Awareness
sources.access: Publisher abstract; chapter full access restricted

implemented: Author reports game-playing implementation and metareasoning for selection, prioritization and stopping of learning.
learned: Problem-class expertise through practice and apprenticeship; heuristic prioritization.
designed: Initial domain knowledge, architecture of cooperating heuristics, learning and evaluation machinery.
limit: Neither unrestricted invention of goals nor independently evolved learning mechanisms established; chapter full methods not acquired.
ora: Distinguish learned selection among strategies from the origin of the strategies and evaluative machinery.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.authors: Stuart C. Shapiro; Jonathan P. Bona
sources.title: The GLAIR Cognitive Architecture
sources.access: Open access CC BY 4.0, abstract and publisher metadata reviewed

implemented: Authors describe embodied agents with belief, grounding and sensor-actuator layers.
learned: Persistent autonomous acquisition of new grounding mechanisms not established by inspected abstract.
designed: Layered representation, symbolic reasoning, grounding interfaces and actuator controllers.
limit: Functional architecture for embodied reasoning; no inference of phenomenal consciousness or self-created cognitive infrastructure.
ora: Distinguish representation grounding engineered by designers from relations acquired through interaction.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.title: A basic agent
sources.access: Public university-hosted author paper, text inspected; p.42 screenshot unavailable (DisabledError); copyright not inferred

implemented: Author reports a simulated submarine agent integrating language, planning, perception, episodic recall and replanning.
learned: Stores events experienced during operation; accepts externally communicated information.
designed: Simulated symbolic world, limited grammar and lexicon, planner, memory and reflective processes.
limit: Printed p.42 explicitly says inductive learning was not integrated. No physical operation or autonomous acquisition of learning machinery established.
ora: Episodic memory and temporally appropriate behaviour are not sufficient evidence of induction or new cognitive skill acquisition.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.title: Learning Recursive Control Programs from Problem Solving
sources.access: Public publisher PDF, sections 1 and 5 selected methods; pp.509,510,516 visually checked; author copyright

sources.title: Cognitive Architectures and General Intelligent Systems
sources.access: Publisher abstract, free to read; full methods not reviewed

implemented: Reported incremental recursive skill construction from successful problem-solving traces in three domains; comparison with learning disabled in Blocks World.
learned: Executable hierarchical procedures that generalize to more objects in familiar goals; prior skills become components of later ones.
designed: Primitive actions and effects, concepts, goals, search and goal-driven composition algorithm.
limit: Fixed domain primitives and supplied goal concepts; bounded search comparator; no independent replication. Transfer to arbitrarily specified new goal structures remains a limitation (p.515).
ora: Important positive comparator for independently composed skills; distinguish structural composition, efficiency, goal generalization and evolution of the learner itself.
funding_boundary: All three identifiers visually confirmed in p.516 acknowledgement; award recipient and administrative completion not established by paper alone.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.title: Workload Warriors: Lessons Learned from a Decade of Mental Workload Prediction Using Human Performance Modeling
sources.access: Publisher abstract; full methods not reviewed

sources.title: Human Performance Modeling Architecture with HC-130J Mission Application
sources.access: Publisher text, selected methods; no independent verification
sources.institution: Human Factors and Ergonomics Society proceedings

implemented: Task-network discrete-event model predicts human workload; later research applies a model-based workflow to a crew case study.
learned: No autonomous acquisition of cognitive competencies established.
designed: Task networks, workload estimates, resource interfaces and operator allocations supplied by modelers.
limit: Predicts human performance rather than demonstrating cognition of an artificial agent; model prediction not equivalent to empirical validation or metabolic cost.
ora: Useful negative comparator: resource-constrained simulation is not inherently a learning organism.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.
